sources_read: Workbook Quality Checks A28:D28 and Internal Quality Checks A28:E28; both quality sheets and Deterministic Checks read completely.
evidence: Reverse-mapped all 94 criteria (80 Functional, 6 Polish, 6 Visual, 2 gates) against frozen public requirements; map and source hashes: qc/runs/coldwater-2026-10-01-history-hardening-r2/evidence/27/source-audit.json. Two instances enforce a transport detail the public ask does not: tests/scored/functional/prompt.md:470 requires "Repeat that exact captured restore request once" and again after a later Save; :433 requires replaying the "exact successful restore request" after restart. These feed cw_restore_retry (judge.toml:532) and cw_restore_retry_restart (:581). Public behaviour.md:38 requires retrying the same attempt and returning its original result; :40 requires durable recognition; policy.md:5 leaves API routes and request fields free. Neither requires old consumed/expired transport metadata to remain valid. The executable local counterexample returns original revision 3 for the same attempt using a fresh anti-CSRF token before/after newer revision 4 and database reopen, leaves history exactly [1,2,3,4], but rejects byte-identical old-token replay. Log: qc/runs/coldwater-2026-10-01-history-hardening-r2/evidence/27/restore_retry_counterexample.log. All 60 indexed raw artifacts matched their current SHA256; no configured-judge result is inferred.
counterexample: A local shared-library app stores restore attempts durably and refreshes a one-use anti-CSRF nonce for each HTTP attempt. Its UI retries preserve the logical attempt identifier and return the original restore result without mutation, including after a newer Save or process restart. Replaying the original complete request uses a consumed nonce and correctly receives a transport-freshness refusal; the two criteria would fail a publicly conforming retry implementation. The executable backend model illustrates this boundary; it is not a complete app evaluation.
suggested_fix: Preserve the restore-attempt identity, target and original base revision, but allow refreshing observed transport/session/anti-CSRF metadata before retries; verify the original committed result and unchanged head/history, retaining the real UI lost-reply retry check.
